guide.title: How to get a sign-in file
guide.step1: In Chrome or Edge, install "Get cookies.txt LOCALLY" and allow it in private windows.
guide.step2: Open a private window, sign in to YouTube, open youtube.com/robots.txt in the same tab and export the file with the extension.
guide.step3: Close the private window (so the sign-in stays valid), then come back and select "Import file".
guide.warning: Make sure the name includes "LOCALLY". Older extensions with similar names have security concerns.
guide.firefox: Use Firefox? Just choose "Use Firefox sign-in"; no export needed.

notice.title: Before using a sign-in file
notice.point1: This file is your YouTube sign-in. Never share it.
notice.point2: It's stored encrypted on this computer and used only for downloads, never uploaded. You can remove it anytime.
notice.point3: YouTube may restrict accounts used this way. Use a separate account and avoid downloading a lot at once.
notice.point4: The sign-in expires after a few weeks. Import it again when it does.
